zionBlackout.label: Blackout
zionBlackout.note: BLACKOUT. The transport was interrupted here. Hold the ground and it will finish the crossing.
zionBlackout.intro: BATTLE. Machines and raiders are coming for the core. Hold it through three waves: fight them off, use the cover, and take out the turrets.
zionBlackout.name: Blackout

zionHideout.label: Gang Hideout
zionHideout.note: The gang’s own room. Whatever is in the chair at the far end is not asleep.
zionHideout.intro: The gang’s own room. Whatever is in the chair at the far end is not asleep.
zionHideout.name: Zion Gang Hideout

zionSpacedock.label: Zion Spacedock
zionSpacedock.note: High above Zion. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
zionSpacedock.intro: High above Zion. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
zionSpacedock.name: Zion Spacedock

npcs.name: Maren
npcs.greeting: Pans on the left, everything you actually need on the right.
npcs.bio: Keeps the shop on the square. Half her stock is for the river and the other half is for people who have just come off it.

npcs.name: Dorkin
npcs.greeting: Same steel goes into a truck and into a breastplate. Ask for either.
npcs.bio: Beats plate in a room the size of a cellar and fabricates half the arena's roll cages on the side.

npcs.name: Odessa
npcs.greeting: Sit anywhere. Boots on the rail, not on the bench.
npcs.bio: Runs the tavern by the crossing. Settles arena bets across the bar and has never once been asked twice for the total.

npcs.name: Ripley
npcs.greeting: Tokens here. Tilt it and you buy the table.
npcs.bio: Runs the change desk and the machines behind it. Can tell you the high score on every table and who is about to lose it.

npcs.name: Bex
npcs.greeting: Mind the jack stands. Everything in here is heavier than it looks.
npcs.bio: Runs the shop that keeps the arena trucks running. Currently has one up on stands with a wheel off and opinions about whose fault it was.

npcs.name: Vance
npcs.greeting: Floor is yours if you want it. Say the word and I let them out.
npcs.bio: Runs the card, works the pit gate and keeps one truck fuelled for whoever is daft enough to take the floor. Has seen every way this goes wrong and will not be told.

npcs.name: Zada

lines.text: Zada.
You crossed the square, so you have seen the crest. Everything here is measured from it.
River south, hills west, arena east. Whichever you pick, come back and tell me what you found.

npcs.bio: Holds Zion, the river rights and the arena licence, and says the middle one is the only one anybody argues about.

npcs.name: Captain Boone

lines.text: Captain.
The scrap on the runs was machinery once. Something up there is putting it back together wrong.
Fight it on the flat. On a slope it only has to lean on you.

npcs.bio: Runs the barracks and the hill patrol. Lost two trucks on the upper run and will not discuss the second one.

npcs.name: Zoran

lines.text: You work the river?
Four bends, south to north, and back again when the light goes. It pays about as well as it sounds.
There is scrap walking about down there now. It came off the hills and it does not pan for anything.
Why not take a claim?
A claim is a stake in one bend. I would rather know all of them.
Besides, a claim gives the assay office an opinion about me.

npcs.bio: Works the gold river and knows which bends are worth a morning. Has been offered a claim three times and taken none of them.

npcs.name: Zell

lines.text: You drive the arena?
When the card is good. This forecourt is where I find out whether it is — everything rolls through here first.
You can tell a serious night by how quiet the crews are on the apron.
What is in the arena?
Something they built out of everything the arena has ever broken. It stands up out of the wreck pile.
Do not fight it in the middle. Put the stands at your back and make it come to you.

npcs.bio: Zion's arena driver, and the only one who has taken the Crusher's gate twice. Rebuilds her own truck between cards and sleeps in the yard.

npcs.name: Hoyt

lines.text: Good bend today?
The second one. It always gives on a bright morning and never on a grey one, and nobody has ever explained that to me.
Do not work the fourth. Whatever came off the hills goes down to drink there.

npcs.bio: Panned the river forty years and has opinions about all four bends. Comes in at noon and leaves when the lamps are lit.

npcs.name: Sable

lines.text: You work the arena?
The pit lane. I see about nine seconds of every event and I could not tell you who won any of them.
If you take a truck out there, come to the shop first. Bex will sell you tyres. Buy the tyres.

npcs.bio: Changes tyres for whoever is driving the card that night and has never once watched the finish.

npcs.name: Nel

lines.text: Winning?
Against the board, always. Against Bram, never. He does not even look at it.

topics.label: What is on the hill runs?
replies: Scrap that stands up. It was machinery once and something is putting it back together wrong.
Boone lost two trucks up there. Ask him about the first one; he will not discuss the second.

topics.label: Anything past the summit?
replies: A gang yard, and they shoot at anything with an engine.
They pop up from behind the drums, take a shot, and duck. Half of them soak two.

topics.label: Good throwing, then.
replies: Mm. Shut the door on your way past, it whistles.

npcs.bio: Barracks trooper, three throws from the record on that board, and will tell you so.

npcs.name: Ida

lines.text: Same four songs.
They are the good ones. If I found a fifth I would play five.
Odessa turns it down when the place fills. I turn it back up. That is the arrangement.

npcs.bio: Feeds the machine coin after coin and plays the same four songs in the same order.

npcs.name: Pross

lines.text: You take the hill road?
I used to. Now I take it as far as the second switchback and turn round, and I sleep fine about it.

topics.label: Who is up there?
replies: A gang, on the summit, in a yard behind a fence.
They do not chase. They wait behind whatever is nearest and stand up when you are past it.

topics.label: What is inside the hideout?
replies: The one who takes the cut. Big, and he does not come out to the yard.
Clear the yard from a distance first. Whatever you carry, carry something that reaches.

topics.label: Thanks.
replies: Buy your own next time.

npcs.bio: Runs cargo up the hill road when the road is worth running, which lately it is not.

npcs.name: Verna

lines.text: Busy in here.
It is one counter for the whole of Zion. Maren could hire somebody and will not.
Batteries are on the right. Everything on the left is for people who like pans.

npcs.bio: Buys for the whole crossing and argues about every line of it.

npcs.name: Pip

lines.text: What are you after?
Lamp oil, a spool, and a bag of the yellow ones. The yellow ones are for me.
If you are going to the parlour, the ZION table is the easy one. Do not tell Ripley I said easy.

npcs.bio: Fetches for three households and is paid in whatever is on the prize shelf next door.

npcs.name: Ordell

lines.text: Heavy work.
Downhill both ways if you go the long way round, which I do.
Odessa counts them at her end. She has never once made it come out the same as me.

npcs.bio: Rolls the tavern's barrels down from here twice a week and counts it as his exercise.

npcs.name: Sten

lines.text: Trouble with the kit?
Something on the upper run put a dent in a plate that is not supposed to dent.
Same steel goes into a truck, he says. It also comes out of one the same way.

npcs.bio: Waiting on a hinge Dorkin has promised twice. Has been waiting since the morning.

npcs.name: Marrow

lines.text: Busy stone.
Busier since the hills went bad. Half of what comes across it now is somebody's wrench.
Bring me anything with an edge. I will not touch a raygun, so do not ask.

npcs.bio: Puts an edge on anything anyone brings in and charges by the length, not by the hour.

npcs.name: Corle

lines.text: Are those for sale?
None of them. Every one came off somebody who walked back in without it.
The bare hook on the end is the Captain's second truck. He asked us to leave it bare.

npcs.bio: Dusts the shield wall, straightens it, and considers it a post rather than a chore.

npcs.name: Kell

lines.text: Any good?
The bank lights both ramps on this one. Everybody goes for the crest ramp. The upper pays the same and it is easier.
Nudge it and Ripley appears out of the floor. I have tested this.

npcs.bio: Learned every table in here in a fortnight and has been stuck on HILL RUN ever since.

npcs.name: Jonty

lines.text: It is dark.
That is the table. It stays dark until you take the gate, and then it pays you an extra ball for the trouble.
They built it after the pylon field went out. Somebody thought that was funny.

npcs.bio: Only ever plays BLACKOUT, and only ever with the marquee off.

npcs.name: Ruse

lines.text: What are you saving for?
Top row. Do not look at it, you will want it, and then it will cost more.
Ripley restocks on a Tuesday. Nothing good has ever appeared on a Tuesday.

npcs.bio: Saving tokens for the top shelf and will not say which thing on it.

npcs.name: Tolliver

lines.text: Nine years?
Nine. Straight coin, no tricks, that table. No ramps to hide behind.
Whoever took it did it in one visit and never came back. That is the part I mind.

npcs.bio: Held the house record on THE ASSAY for nine years and lost it in March to a stranger.

npcs.name: Gus

lines.text: What is wrong with that one?
Rear left is off, hub is bare, and the lug nuts are on the floor where I can see them.
The other one is on the lift and finished. It is finished because nobody has driven it yet.

npcs.bio: Bex's second pair of hands. Walks the pit lane between the two trucks all day and calls it thinking.

npcs.name: Tam

lines.text: Yours?
The far one was. It is parts now. Bex says that is a stage and not a verdict.
Rent one if you are going up the hill. Renting is cheaper than what I have done.

npcs.bio: Brought a truck in three weeks ago and has come to look at it every day since.

npcs.name: Halder

lines.text: What is on the bench?
Everything anybody owes. Most of it is Tam and I have stopped writing his name.
Upgrades go on the truck, not on the shelf. Ask Bex, she does the fitting.

npcs.bio: Fetches from the shelf, writes it on the bench in chalk, and rubs it out when it is paid.

npcs.name: Sergeant Ovie

lines.text: Sergeant.
Feet outside the ring or in it. There is no third place to stand.

topics.label: How do I fight the scrap?
replies: On the flat, and never with your back to a slope.
The big ones wind up before they swing. That is your whole opening; take it or move.

topics.label: What is the cage for?
replies: Learning where your feet go when somebody is trying to put you down.
Everything else is a story you tell afterwards.

topics.label: Understood.
replies: Good. Mind the dummies, they are heavier than they look.

npcs.bio: Runs the sparring cage and the morning drill, and has never once been seen on the hill runs.

npcs.name: Trooper Bram

lines.text: Nel says you never miss.
Nel says a lot at that board and none of it while she is throwing.
Sit if you want. Nothing here is anybody's seat except the Captain's.

npcs.bio: Eats at the same end of the same table and throws darts without looking at the board.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Fenn

lines.text: What is in there?
What is left. Two racks went up the hill this season and one rack came back.
If you find our kit out there on something that is walking about, it is still ours.

npcs.bio: Counts the vault twice a day and signs for it both times, which he says is the whole job.

npcs.name: Trooper Kiln

lines.text: Long aisle.
Six bunks, all on this side, so the lane stays clear from the door to the hall.
That was deliberate. You will be glad of it if anything ever gets in here.

npcs.bio: Walks the bunk aisle end to end on the night watch and does it in daylight too, out of habit.

npcs.name: Guard Ansel

lines.text: Quiet post.
It is Zada's hall. If it is loud in here something has gone very wrong somewhere else.
Walk up the middle. The nave is for walking up.

npcs.bio: West alcove, every day, and has developed strong views about the draught in it.

npcs.name: Guard Rook

lines.text: Anything through here?
Assay clerks, mostly, and whoever is arguing about the river that week.
The door behind me is not a way through. Ask Fenn at the barracks if you want a vault.

npcs.bio: East alcove, and keeps the treasury door in the corner of her eye without ever turning to it.

npcs.name: Clerk Pell

lines.text: Clerk.
One moment. These have to be read out before they can be sealed, and they have to be sealed today.

topics.label: What does the assay do?
replies: Weighs what comes off the river and says what it is worth, and the saying is the part people fight about.
Zada holds the seal. Everything else here is arithmetic.

topics.label: Is the river still good?
replies: The take is down a fifth on the season and it is not the water.
Panners have stopped working the far bends. You can guess why as well as I can.

topics.label: I will let you read.
replies: Thank you. Mind the medallion, people do slip on it.

npcs.bio: Carries the week's river weights up the nave and reads them out whether or not anyone is listening.

npcs.name: Herald Ame

lines.text: Do I need announcing?
You are already most of the way up, so it would be for form. I will do it anyway.
Zada is at the dais. She will have seen you come in; she always does.

npcs.bio: Walks the east side of the nave announcing people who are already halfway up it.

npcs.name: Marn

lines.text: Long road.
It is. Keep west of the tyre stacks and you will not meet anything coming down.

npcs.bio: Walks the arena road end to end and counts the trucks going up.

npcs.name: Pell

lines.text: Is it on tonight?
Vance has the floor live. Do not walk in — she will not stop it for you.

npcs.bio: Minds the forecourt on arena nights and shoos people off the gate.

npcs.name: Tarn

lines.text: Busy?
Somebody clips a drum every single night. I sweep it up every single morning.

npcs.bio: Sweeps the approach after every run and has opinions about the drums.

npcs.name: Guard Halden

lines.text: Anything up the north road?
Castle path. Quiet today. It is quiet most days, which is the job working.
Nice helmet.
Zada's issue. Shield on the chest, Z on the banner. You will not mistake us.

npcs.bio: Holds the north gate of the square and has never once been asked to move.

npcs.name: Guard Vess

lines.text: Long shift?
Halden talks, I watch. Between us the gate is covered.
Trouble ever?
A truck came down the avenue sideways once. Once was plenty.

npcs.bio: The other half of the north gate, and the half that actually watches.

npcs.name: Guard Corbin

lines.text: Walking the square?
West column. Up, down, up. You learn every loose cobble on it.
Seen the citizens about?
In gold, same as me. Difference is they get to stop and talk.

npcs.bio: Walks the west column of the square top to bottom, every hour of the day.

npcs.name: Guard Ryn

lines.text: What are you keeping clear?
The pad. The Z is worth looking at and hard to see under a parked truck.
Fair.
Walk it slow when you cross. That is all I ask of anybody.

npcs.bio: Crosses the front of the plaza east to west and keeps the crest clear.

npcs.name: Guard Brac

lines.text: Can I go up?
Gate is open. Mind the drums on the apron, they are not decoration.
You ever drive?
I stand. Standing has a better record.

npcs.bio: West side of the arena gate. Counts every truck up and every truck back.

npcs.name: Guard Toft

lines.text: Busy up there?
A run on. You will hear it before you see it.
Anything I should know?
Come back down the same road you went up. Saves me finding you.

npcs.bio: East side of the arena gate, and the one who waves the wrecks back down.

npcs.name: Guard Nesk

lines.text: Can I go up?
Zada's hall is open to Zion. Walk up the middle and mind the plinths.
Who am I looking for?
Zada herself. Herald Ame will announce you if she is in a mood to.

npcs.bio: West of the castle gate, and has stood there long enough to know every cart that comes up the road by the sound of it.

npcs.name: Guard Dorrin

lines.text: Quiet up here?
Quiet is the whole job. Loud means I did it badly.
What is the ditch?
Dry moat, whole width of the hill. One bridge. That is not an accident.

npcs.bio: East of the castle gate. Watches the bridge over the dry moat and the barracks fork below it.

npcs.name: Odette

lines.text: Any chance you are looking for a job? We got great croissants here, super fun to make.

topics.label: How do I make croissants?
replies: Six things, in order, and none of them forgive you for the last one.
Lock a slab of butter inside the dough. Then roll it out and fold it in three, three times over — that is one, three, nine, twenty-seven layers.
Cut triangles, roll them up from the wide end. Prove them until they are ready and not a minute past. Then bake them to the shade on the order.
That is the whole trade. The hard part is that it is all timing.

topics.label: How did you get into the baking business?
replies: My mother ran a bread oven at the gold camp. Miners came off the river at four in the morning wanting something hot, and she was the only one up.
I did the fires from when I was small. Learned the laminating off a book that came in wrapping a crate of nails.
Took me nine months to get one right. Then Zada ate one and asked who made it, and that was the shop.

topics.label: Not just now.
replies: The oven will still be hot. Come back when you want your paws floury.

npcs.bio: Runs the bakery on the square. Up at three, laminating by four, and still cheerful about it at noon.

npcs.name: Wick

lines.text: If you are working water on this river, I would rather it was written down. Saves the arguing later.

topics.label: What does a claim get me?
replies: The bar is yours to work while you hold it. A third more to the pan, and nobody else standing in your riffle.
One at a time. You want the middle reach instead, you give me back the north bar first, and I strike it out in front of you.
That is the whole of it. The register is not the law. It is just the only thing between two people and an argument.

topics.label: Who else is on the book?
replies: Nobody, at the minute. Half the camp went up the hill after the trucks and the other half went home to think about it.
Which is the best time to file, if you are asking me sideways.

topics.label: Why is it spelled SURVAY?
replies: The sign painter charged by the letter and could not spell. I was not paying him twice.
Everybody knows where it is.

topics.label: Just looking.
replies: The board is on the wall. Look all you want.

npcs.bio: Keeps the register of every bar on the gold river. Has never once been seen outside the office in daylight.

npcs.name: Cass

lines.text: Busy square.
Arena night. It is always arena night by the time you notice.

npcs.bio: Sweeps the crossing and has views about where the trucks park.

npcs.name: Juno

lines.text: What is south?
The river. Take a pan; the shallows still pay if you are patient.

npcs.bio: Pans the river four mornings a week and calls it a hobby.

npcs.name: Rell

lines.text: What is west?
Hill road, then the runs. Trucks go up them. People mostly do not.

npcs.bio: Sells cold drinks at the arena gate and makes a season's living in a night.

npcs.name: Mika

lines.text: Hello.
Watch the crossing — half the town drives across it and none of them look.

npcs.bio: Was on a pit crew for nine years. Still flinches at a dropped wrench.

npcs.name: Tobe

lines.text: Who runs Zion?
The castle, north. Though on a race night the arena does, honestly.

npcs.bio: Keeps the square's lamps lit and the crest swept.

npcs.name: Wynn

lines.text: Anything to see?
The parlour, if it rains. Best three tables on the planet, and I have seen others.

npcs.bio: Holds the parlour high score on the middle table and mentions it.

npcs.name: Solen

lines.text: Citizen.
Zion keeps you, and you keep Zion. That is the whole of it.

npcs.bio: Keeps the crossing lamps lit and the flags straight. Has done it for eleven years.

npcs.name: Bram

lines.text: Where is the parlour?
Big block, north-east corner. They swapped with the item shop — the shop is in the little one on the south side now.

npcs.bio: Runs errands between the tavern and the armory and knows everybody by their boots.

npcs.name: Ivet

lines.text: Busy tonight?
Vance has the floor on. You can hear it from here if the wind is right.

npcs.bio: Sells flags on arena nights and opinions on all the others.

npcs.name: Dala

lines.text: Good day.
And to you. Mind the trucks on the east road.

npcs.bio: A citizen of Zion. Wears the gold and keeps to the square.

npcs.name: Kesh

lines.text: Anything worth knowing?
The drums by the arena ramps go up if you clip them. Ask me how I know.

npcs.bio: Walks the south side twice a day and calls it keeping an eye on things.

npcs.name: Oro

lines.text: Good day.
And to you. Mind the trucks on the east road.

npcs.bio: A citizen of Zion. Wears the gold and keeps to the square.

lines.text: Welcome to Zion, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.
